title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $12.03: 24 and 13 units (vs baseline 18.9), suggesting demand elasticity. No past price increase at this level, but pattern implies ~12% reduction.

adjustment.analysis: No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 6.2% above regular, which typically suppresses demand. The last two weeks at $12.03 saw 24 and 13 units—below baseline (18.9), suggesting price sensitivity. Heatwave (38°C) may boost demand, but no historical heatwave effect is recorded. Past promotions show a 1.4x lift, but the current price is higher, not lower. The classical model's 1.00 multiplier is plausible, but the price increase warrants downward adjustment. Evidence is thin, so shrink toward 1.0. No seasonal or trend signal. Confidence is medium.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.9 | 5%-95%: 6.2 - 35.5 | 10%-90%: 9.5 - 31.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
